title.value: THE EFFECT SIZE OF GENES ON COGNITIVE ABILITIES IS LINKED TO THEIR EXPRESSION ALONG THE MAJOR HIERARCHICAL GRADIENT IN THE HUMAN BRAIN
title.justification: The paper's title explicitly states a focus on understanding how the effect size of genes on cognitive abilities correlates with their expression along a hierarchical gradient in the brain.
title.quote: THE EFFECT SIZE OF GENES ON COGNITIVE ABILITIES IS LINKED TO THEIR EXPRESSION ALONG THE MAJOR HIERARCHICAL GRADIENT IN THE HUMAN BRAIN

analysis.description: This paper investigates the relationship between gene expression and cognitive abilities, focusing on how genetic variations such as copy number variants (CNVs) affect cognition. It specifically examines the spatial and temporal expression patterns of genes in the brain and their impact on intelligence, using data from large cohorts.

type.justification: The paper involves the analysis of large-scale datasets and presents empirical evidence on the effect size of genes on cognition.
type.quote: Results: We observed significant effects of over half of the coding genes on cognitive abilities and mapped effect sizes for these individual coding genes.
